prerequisites: Estadística, Ampliación de Cálculo y Teoría de Circuitos

learning_outcomes.text: Correctly and fluently handle the logarithmic units of power, gain, and attenuation used in communication systems (CR.4, CG.3, CG.5, CG.6).
Apply the fundamentals of time and frequency domain analysis to solve problems in communication systems (CR.4, CR.5, CG.3, CG.4).

Characterize information, both as a signal and as a stochastic process, to be transmitted by a communication system, as well as the disturbances that limit the performance of said system (CR.4, CR.5, CG.3, CG.4).
Describe and distinguish the functional blocks of analog and digital communication systems (CR.1, CR.4, CR.5, CG.3, CG.5, CG.6).
Obtain the fundamental parameters of analog and digital communication systems (CR.4, CG.3, CG.5, CG.6).
Understand the limitations and performance of different analog and digital modulation systems (CR.5, CG.3, CG.5, CG.6).

Conveniently evaluate the trade-off between bandwidth and power consumption to obtain a certain quality in a given configuration of an analog or digital communication system (CR.1, CR.5, CR.15, CG.4, CG.5, CG.6).
Understand the main analog and digital modulation techniques to identify the most appropriate technique in a given transmission configuration (CR.1, CR.5, CG.3, CG.5, CG.6).
Discuss and evaluate in a group the most appropriate analog and/or digital modulation technique under given operating conditions and restrictions (CR.1, CR.5, CG.4, CG.9).

Apply knowledge of the different technological alternatives for deploying communication systems to functionally design systems that meet certain pre-imposed requirements and performance (CR.1, CR.5, CR.6, CR.15, CG.2, CG.3, CG.4, CG.6).

syllabus_topics: Characterization of signals and information signaling in baseband
Physical signals and their mathematical models
Characteristic parameters of signals: voltage, power, energy and their logarithmic units
Energy Spectral Density (ESD) and Power Spectral Density (PSD)
Bandwidth
Correlation between signals
Autocorrelation
Uncorrelation, orthogonality and incoherence
Stochastic process: mathematical model and interpretation
Statistical averages: mathematical expectation, correlation function and covariance function
Independence, uncorrelation and orthogonality
Stationarity and ergodicity
Power and spectral characterization of processes
Gaussian random processes
Characterization of thermal noise as a random process
Characterization of filtered random processes
Information signaling in baseband
Analog voice, audio and video signals
Analog modulations using pulsed signals: PAM, PWM and PPM
Quantization of analog signals
Digital pulsed modulations: PCM
Symbol and bit energy, spectral density and efficiency
Communication systems with baseband transmission
Introduction
General model of a communication system
Introduction to the concepts of channel sharing and information multiplexing
Quality parameters
Resources of a communication system
Characterization of systems in time and frequency
Attenuation, gain and logarithmic units (decibel dB)
Characterization of filtered signals
Linear distortion: amplitude and phase distortion
Non-linear distortion: harmonic distortion and intermodulation distortion
Definition of noise: thermal noise
White noise
Representation of noise in a communication system: equivalent noise bandwidth, equivalent noise temperature and noise factor
Friis' Formula
Transmission of analog baseband signals and reception in the presence of noise
Signal-to-noise ratio
Transmission of pulsed baseband signals and receivers in the presence of noise
Intersymbol interference (ISI)
Bayesian decision
Optimal digital receiver implementation in Gaussian channel
Shannon's Theorem
Representation of noise in the signal space
Calculation of error probability and properties
Communication systems with passband transmission
Passband signals and passband stochastic processes: complex envelope and phasor diagram
Passband noise
Low-pass equivalent of a system
Modulation: modulation objectives, spectral and power efficiency
Analog modulations: amplitude, phase and frequency modulations
Definition, spectral and power analysis
Introduction to single-carrier digital amplitude, phase and frequency modulations for passband transmission
Passband communication system model
Transmission and Reception Schemes: Direct receiver, superheterodyne
Quality analysis in predetection and postdetection
Receiver sensitivity
Signal-to-noise ratio
Probability of error in digital systems
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade (Nf) is calculated as 0.7 * Ef + 0.3 * Ep, where Ef is the final written exam and Ep is the lab practices evaluation. The lab practices evaluation will be a written test on concepts handled with simulators, performed individually or in pairs during lab sessions. For extraordinary calls and differentiated evaluation, the final grade is calculated using the same formula; students can choose to replace the practical evaluation with the grade obtained during the semester. In case of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, students may be asked for an in-person defense.
